name: dom-manipulation
description: A script that manipulates the DOM in various ways.

variants.javascript-no-comments: Write a JavaScript script that demonstrates DOM manipulation. The script should be enclosed in a function. It should create a new `div` element with the text "Hello, World!", add it to the body of the page, and then update its text to "Hello, DOM!" after 2 seconds. The script should not have any comments.
variants.javascript-inline-comments: Write a JavaScript script that demonstrates DOM manipulation. The script should be enclosed in a function. It should create a new `div` element with the text "Hello, World!", add it to the body of the page, and then update its text to "Hello, DOM!" after 2 seconds. The script should include inline comments to explain the logic.
variants.javascript-jsdoc: Write a JavaScript script that demonstrates DOM manipulation. The script should be enclosed in a function. It should create a new `div` element with the text "Hello, World!", add it to the body of the page, and then update its text to "Hello, DOM!" after 2 seconds. The script should include JSDoc comments for the main function.
variants.javascript-vanilla-web-jsdoc: Write a vanilla JavaScript script that demonstrates DOM manipulation. The script should be enclosed in a function. It should create a new `div` element with the text "Hello, World!", add it to the body of the page, and then update its text to "Hello, DOM!" after 2 seconds. The script should include JSDoc comments for the main function.
variants.typescript-react-no-comments: Write a TypeScript React component that demonstrates DOM manipulation. The component should render a `div` element with the text "Hello, World!". After 2 seconds, the text should be updated to "Hello, DOM!". The component should not have any comments.
variants.typescript-react-tsdoc: Write a TypeScript React component that demonstrates DOM manipulation. The component should render a `div` element with the text "Hello, World!". After 2 seconds, the text should be updated to "Hello, DOM!". The component should include TSDoc comments for the component and its props.

testCases.test: async () => { await page.waitForSelector('div'); const div = await page.$('div'); const initialText = await div.textContent(); console.assert(initialText === 'Hello, World!', 'Initial text should be Hello, World!'); await page.waitForTimeout(2000); const updatedText = await div.textContent(); console.assert(updatedText === 'Hello, DOM!', 'Text should be updated to Hello, DOM!'); }
